title: The Medicare Part D Yearly Drug Cost Cap, Explained Simply
bigPicture: Medicare drug plans (Part D) have a yearly limit on what you pay out of pocket for covered drugs. In 2026 it is $2,100.
whatYouNeedToKnow: The yearly out-of-pocket cap for Part D drugs is $2,100 in 2026 and $2,400 in 2027. It changes from year to year.
It applies to covered drugs in a Medicare Part D drug plan.
After any deductible and 25% coinsurance, you reach the cap and move to catastrophic coverage.
Once you reach the cap, you pay nothing out of pocket for covered Part D drugs for the rest of the calendar year.
What you spend on covered Part D drugs counts toward the cap, including certain payments made on your behalf, such as through Extra Help.
The Medicare Prescription Payment Plan can spread your drug costs across the calendar year to help with monthly budgeting. It does not save you money or lower your drug costs.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Assuming the cap is the same every year. It is $2,100 in 2026 and $2,400 in 2027.
Assuming every drug counts. Only covered Part D drugs count toward the cap.
Thinking the payment plan lowers your costs. It only spreads them out.
actionSteps: Check that your medicines are covered by your Part D plan.
Keep track of what you spend on covered drugs during the year.
If large drug bills worry you, read about the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan on Medicare.gov.
Review your drug plan each year, since the cap and plan costs change.
